parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal statute, no documented arrests, raids, facility bans or custody-placement rules affecting visitors. The operative exposures are state censorship and a hostile institutional climate: derisive immigration handling of a trans visitor (documented, no recourse), rainbow-expression bans extending to foreigners, platform scrubbing, and conversion therapy still routine with no protective machinery. Severity if outed is mostly tier-2/3 (humiliation, discrimination, expression repression) rather than tier-1/2 custody exposure. A narrow court remedy exists (2024 conversion-therapy payout), showing some functioning recourse. Sits above the 0.35 anchors (no universal-exposure register/reporting regime) but below 0.65 anchors, whose visitors faced isolated friction within protective frameworks; here protections are absent and the climate is contracting.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented mocking and intrusive questioning of a trans visitor by immigration officers (May 2025); no formal marker-mismatch rule sourced.
entry_documents.protection: Dependent residency for same-sex partners of residents; no entry bar documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Border humiliation with no stated recourse mechanism.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented for trans visitors; no arrests or detention patterns reported.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Censorship baseline: rainbow flags banned even inside venues, LGBT content scrubbed from platforms (2026), foreign drag performer met shrinking space.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitors' expression and online content fall under national censorship rules.

care_services.exposure: Conversion therapy routine in psychiatric facilities; estradiol/blocker online sales banned (2022), forcing in-person purchase; adult surgery requires parental consent.
care_services.protection: Seven youth clinics and puberty-blocker consensus exist; 2024 court awarded damages for forced conversion.
care_services.interaction: A travelling adult may struggle to refill HRT; minors' access is family-gated.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Crackdown on 'foreign ideologies', activism 'all but extinct', 2016 'abnormal behaviour' broadcast ban extended to platforms; UN vote against SOGI mandate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State frames LGBT expression as disorder, raising outing and censorship exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parental-consent gates and family-dispute pressure affect trans minors and accompanying guardians; sex-segregated schooling discrimination documented for residents.
minors_guardians.protection: One province allows minors' gender-marker change with guardian ID (single data point).
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's minor cannot access gender care without parental/local consent structures.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2018 beating of two women with rainbow badges by security guards — single incident, guards dismissed; no trans-specific violence rate available.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Guards were dismissed, showing some accountability.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Background violence magnitude unknown; cannot rule elevated or baseline.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; NGOs cannot register; entry screening practice for markers unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Narrow court remedy worked for conversion-therapy victim (2024).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is exceptional, not systematic; open questions on documents and custody remain unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia's police systematically stop, detain and fine trans visitors as state practice. This jurisdiction documents no such targeting of visitors — one border humiliation, no detentions — so it rates above it.

Marisol Union's ward assignment by documents parallels this dossier's absence of accommodations, but here the deeper deficit is no protections at all plus active censorship of visitors' expression; slightly below, though no custodial exposure either.

Vellmaris has national equality law, reliable courts and compensation. Here recourse is one narrow win, expression is censored, and institutions are hostile, so it sits below, though no arrest or detention pathway is documented.

Drellia imposes universal registration and database disclosure on every visitor. This jurisdiction has no such universal-exposure mechanism documented; friction and censorship are the operative harms, placing it modestly above.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is censorial rather than carceral toward trans visitors: no criminal statute or arrest pattern is documented, and no universal-exposure measure (registration, facility bans, marker checks) reaches every crossing. The documented exposures — derisive border handling, expression bans applying to foreign performers, platform scrubbing, conversion therapy in routine use, HRT purchase barriers, and no anti-discrimination machinery — are tier-2/3 harms: humiliation, service friction and repression rather than imprisonment. A single functioning court remedy (2024 payout) shows the legal system is not wholly closed, and a 2018 assault produced accountability. Unresolved entry-document screening and thin violence data cap confidence; absence of evidence is not safety. Net placement: elevated risk with reduced severity floor, roughly 0.58.
